US2014211529.headline: Solar inverter that also helps at night
US2014211529.summary: Small inverters attached to individual solar panels normally sit idle once the sun goes down. This design lets the unit run in reverse when no solar power is available, so it can draw power from the grid or help stabilise voltage on the network, making the hardware useful around the clock.

US2014218070.headline: Faster signal bridge between chip voltage levels
US2014218070.summary: Different parts of a chip often run at different voltages, and signals must be converted when crossing between them. This circuit speeds up that conversion by dynamically adjusting the voltage references inside a small memory element, so data moves between low- and high-voltage sections with less delay.

US2014222878.headline: Keeping track of failed file sync attempts
US2014222878.summary: When files are copied between a local computer and remote servers, some updates fail without anyone noticing. This system detects when a change to a file or folder did not go through and records which item was affected, so the problem can be fixed or retried later rather than silently lost.

US2014226967.headline: Smarter backup routes for communication networks
US2014226967.summary: In large telecoms networks, data needs a standby route ready in case a link fails. This method has each network node announce how much bandwidth it needs, which links share a common risk of failing together, and which backup path it would switch to, so the network can plan shared spare capacity more efficiently.

US2014253195.headline: Correcting timing errors in high-speed data links
US2014253195.summary: Fast serial connections between chips rely on a clock signal that can arrive slightly distorted. This approach measures the distortion at the receiving end, works out the correction needed and sends it back to the transmitter in a form it can apply directly, keeping the link accurate without complex feedback loops.

US2014269090.headline: Gentler erasing to prolong flash memory life
US2014269090.summary: Flash memory cells wear out with repeated erasing. This method tracks how heavily each group of cells has been used and, once a threshold is passed, switches to a longer, multi-step erase that is kinder to worn cells, helping storage devices such as SSDs last longer and stay reliable.

US2014280595.headline: Videoconferencing that scales up in the cloud
US2014280595.summary: Video meetings traditionally depend on dedicated hardware that is costly and inflexible. This system mixes physical conferencing equipment with software that imitates it, and uses load-balancing to add or remove capacity as demand changes, so a videoconferencing service can grow or shrink on whatever cloud infrastructure is available.

US2014281875.headline: Shared mark-ups on the same document
US2014281875.summary: Several people often need to comment on one file without altering the original. Here each person's notes are saved as a separate layer, uploaded to cloud storage and then overlaid together on the original document, so everyone sees all annotations at once while the source file stays untouched.

US2014287730.headline: Telling mobile users when streaming will work better
US2014287730.summary: Mobile video can stutter when the network is congested. This system predicts the quality a user is likely to experience before content is delivered and, if it falls short, tells them a time or place where the connection should be good enough, rather than simply serving a poor stream.

US2014295237.headline: Sturdier seal for high-temperature sodium batteries
US2014295237.summary: Sodium metal halide batteries used for grid-scale energy storage run hot and must be sealed tightly. This cell design uses a ceramic collar brazed to a porous metal mesh current collector and sealed to the casing, improving durability and electrical connection inside each cell.

US2014322694.headline: Learning materials that improve from student behaviour
US2014322694.summary: Online courses need to know which lessons actually work. This system watches how many learners interact with a piece of learning content, derives attributes such as difficulty or usefulness from their actions, and keeps those attributes updated so the platform can decide whether and when to offer that lesson to other students.

US2014331001.headline: Orderly handling of admin commands in SSDs
US2014331001.summary: Solid-state drives process a queue of read and write requests while also receiving management instructions that can affect those queues. This method pauses new requests, inserts a marker, finishes the existing work up to the marker and only then applies the management command, avoiding conflicts and data errors.

US2014335498.headline: Automatically creating different versions of an exam
US2014335498.summary: Giving every student an identical test invites copying. This system automatically builds several versions of a test from a question bank, each differing by at least one question, and assigns them to participants according to set rules, then administers the tests, reducing cheating with little extra effort for teachers.

US2014337650.headline: Powering down idle drives in shared storage
US2014337650.summary: Large storage enclosures shared by many servers waste electricity keeping rarely used drives spinning. A power controller monitors how many requests each drive receives over a period and moves quiet drives into a lower-power state, cutting energy use in data centres without affecting busy drives.

US2014350839.headline: Helping a robot know where it is
US2014350839.summary: A mobile robot, such as a vacuum cleaner, must build a map of a room while working out its own position in it. This method keeps many competing guesses about location, each with its own map, updates them with sensor readings, weights them by how well they fit, and picks the best to fix the robot's position.

US2014351589.headline: Logging in by scanning a QR code
US2014351589.summary: Passwords alone are weak protection for online services. Here the server hides a one-off random code inside a QR code shown on screen; the user's phone scans it, unlocks it with a private key stored on the phone and displays a one-time password to type in, giving two-factor security without special hardware.

US2014363870.headline: Yeast that makes copper nanoparticles and cleans wastewater
US2014363870.summary: Producing copper nanoparticles usually needs harsh chemicals, and copper-laden wastewater is a pollution problem. This process uses dead biomass of a common yeast to pull copper out of wastewater and convert it into nanoparticles, offering a cheap, environmentally friendly route that can be scaled up industrially.

US2015005946.headline: Switching fan control to the best sensors
US2015005946.summary: Computers use temperature sensors to decide how hard to run their cooling fans. This method starts with one set of sensors and, depending on the readings, hands fan control over to a different process using another set of sensors, so cooling responds to whichever part of the machine is actually heating up.

US2015012144.headline: Real-time optimisation for mixed power systems
US2015012144.summary: Systems combining several power sources, such as renewables, batteries and generators, are hard to run efficiently over the long term. This controller feeds live measurements and forecasts into a continuously updated optimisation that tells the system how much power to route where and which switches to operate.

US2015056491.headline: Better battery separator that resists clogging
US2015056491.summary: The porous film between a battery's electrodes must let ions through while blocking short circuits. This coating mixes inorganic particles, adhesive and polymer particles that swell by different amounts, forming a smoother layer that is less likely to block the pores, improving ion flow and battery conductivity.

US2015062847.headline: Flexible connector linking parts inside phones
US2015062847.summary: Mobile devices pack components on several faces of a circuit board, which must be electrically joined. This bent metal connector mounts on the board and reaches around to contact parts on adjacent or opposite sides, simplifying assembly in cramped handsets.

US2015067648.headline: Trimming software tests to the ones that matter
US2015067648.summary: Testing software thoroughly is slow and costly. This system gathers details about an application and its test cases, removes redundant or obsolete tests, estimates each remaining test's chance of failure and risk, and uses statistical selection and run-time estimates to produce a smaller, sharper set of tests to run.

US2015067832.headline: Stopping users typing passwords into fake sites
US2015067832.summary: Phishing tricks people into entering sensitive details on impostor websites. Rather than trying to spot the fraudulent message, this approach watches what the user types; if a registered security word such as a password appears, it checks whether the destination is on an approved list and warns if it is not.

US2015100810.headline: Predicting idle time to switch off disk drives
US2015100810.summary: Spinning down an idle hard drive saves power, but doing so just before it is needed costs time. This controller records how long past idle periods lasted, groups them into time windows and, when a drive goes quiet, uses the most common pattern to predict whether the pause will be long enough to justify powering down.

US2015103593.headline: Safeguarding data while moving it in flash memory
US2015103593.summary: Flash storage often shifts data from one memory block to another. This method checks the health of the destination block after writing and, if it looks faulty, keeps the original copy and its address mapping in place, so data is not lost to a failing block.

US2015112690.headline: Low-power wake word for sleeping devices
US2015112690.summary: Listening for a spoken wake-up phrase around the clock can drain a device's battery. Here a tiny always-on circuit screens microphone input for a likely match, then wakes a dedicated audio processor to confirm it before the main processor is roused, keeping standby power very low.

US2015117495.headline: Cheaper, more accurate on-chip thermometers
US2015117495.summary: Temperature sensors built into chips are affected by manufacturing variations between transistors. This method uses the transistors' own characteristics to calculate and cancel out those imperfections, calibrating each part individually and avoiding the need for an expensive external reference thermometer.

US2015130915.headline: 3D glasses with built-in depth control
US2015130915.summary: Stereoscopic video can feel too deep or too flat for individual viewers. These glasses include a control on the frame that adjusts a parameter of the 3D image pair, letting the wearer tune the depth effect directly rather than through the television or player.

US2015134954.headline: Birth certificates for connected devices
US2015134954.summary: Networks of smart sensors need to know each device is genuine before trusting it. This method registers a digital birth certificate tied to a private key for each device, uses it to authenticate the device and then allows the device to be reconfigured physically, logically or in its mode of operation.

US2015138876.headline: Faster, more reliable writes to memory chips
US2015138876.summary: Writing data into on-chip memory becomes harder as transistors shrink. This design uses a shared global wire that is toggled just before and after a write to give the local wire a brief negative voltage boost, helping the memory cell flip state reliably at low power.

US2015142545.headline: Automatic early-payment discounts on invoices
US2015142545.summary: Suppliers often want to be paid sooner and customers want a discount for paying early. This system uses a rules engine to automatically make or accept discount offers on invoices, adjusting the terms based on factors such as the offeror's account balance, encouraging faster payment.

US2015156143.headline: Using phone edge screens to save power
US2015156143.summary: Phones with displays along their edges can show notifications without lighting up the main screen. By giving side screens their own display buffers, this approach lets them show content while the main display and other components stay asleep, saving battery and processing power.

US2015168465.headline: Estimating conditions across an electricity distribution grid
US2015168465.summary: Distribution networks have few sensors, so operators cannot see conditions at every point. This method uses measured current and power flows to estimate loads at each node, compares the resulting voltage estimates with actual readings and adjusts the load estimates until they agree, giving a more accurate picture of the grid.

US2015179918.headline: Cleaner surfaces for quantum computing circuits
US2015179918.summary: Josephson junctions, the building blocks of superconducting quantum chips, are sensitive to contamination. This process etches away oxides and residues from the exposed superconducting electrode using a plasma, then immediately deposits the junction's thin barrier layer in the same sealed chamber, avoiding recontamination.

US2015188900.headline: Keeping users logged in across data centres
US2015188900.summary: Online services spread over several data centres must recognise a user's session wherever it lands. A gateway checks each request with a key, routes it to the nearest data centre, which creates an encrypted token recording where the session lives; that token then travels with later requests so they reach the right place.

US2015205269.headline: Clearer dashboard for advanced plant controllers
US2015205269.summary: Industrial plants rely on controllers that juggle many variables at once, which can be opaque to operators. This system computes indicators showing how each controlled variable relates to the process variables affecting it and displays them together on screen, helping operators monitor and understand the controller's behaviour.

US2015205636.headline: Jumping the queue to speed up a processor
US2015205636.summary: When a computer running slowly to save power needs to speed up, the instruction that raises the clock rate may be stuck behind other tasks. This method finds that task in the pending list and runs it first, so the processor accelerates sooner.

US2015206883.headline: Sturdier capacitors in memory chips
US2015206883.summary: Tall, thin capacitor electrodes in memory chips can lean or collapse during manufacture. This design adds a patterned reinforcing layer with alignment holes through which the electrodes pass, plus a supporting layer above it, keeping the structures upright and properly positioned.

US2015220128.headline: Matching power supply to what circuits need
US2015220128.summary: Digital circuits draw power in bursts timed to a clock signal. This method predicts, for each clock pulse, which elements will actually consume power and adjusts the power supply accordingly, reducing waste and voltage fluctuations in chips and electronic systems.

US2015227452.headline: Generating software tests from business process maps
US2015227452.summary: Writing test cases for business software by hand is slow. This system reads a model of the business process the software supports, identifies test scenarios from it, generates test cases and data for each, and produces automated test scripts from associated keywords.

US2015228045.headline: Hidden watermarks in text documents
US2015228045.summary: Proving the origin of a leaked or copied document is difficult. This method converts each page to an image, crops the margins, divides the page into blocks and embeds an invisible watermark in selected blocks; the same block selection is later used to recover the watermark and trace the document.

US2015231081.headline: Delayed-release tablet for an antifungal drug
US2015231081.summary: Posaconazole, an antifungal medicine, is poorly absorbed in conventional forms. This tablet dissolves the drug in a polymer by hot-melt extrusion so that it is released later in the digestive tract, with the aim of improving how the drug is taken up by the body.

US2015234745.headline: Smarter guessing of data a processor needs next
US2015234745.summary: Processors fetch data in advance to avoid waiting, but wrong guesses waste bandwidth. This controller combines two prefetching strategies with a back-off mechanism that counts whether fetched data is actually used and switches prefetching off when too much goes unused, improving efficiency.

US2015242263.headline: Smoother running of data backup operations
US2015242263.summary: Enterprise backup systems can clog networks and overload servers. This system queues jobs to spread the load, forecasts how long operations will take based on expected throughput between machines, and automatically escalates alerts to someone else if the usual recipient is unavailable.

US2015243563.headline: Transistors with different switching thresholds on one chip
US2015243563.summary: Chips need some transistors that switch easily and others that resist leakage. Here two groups of transistors share the same metal gate material, but the layer is made thicker in one group than the other, producing different switching voltages without additional materials.

US2015274066.headline: Glowing trim panels for car interiors
US2015274066.summary: Car makers want ambient lighting inside vehicles without bulky fittings. This system places a light pipe behind a translucent trim panel so that light passes through the panel into the cabin, creating soft illumination integrated into the interior surfaces.

US2015286629.headline: Spotting names of organisations in any language
US2015286629.summary: Search engines and text tools need to recognise names of companies, places and people in web pages. This system trains machine-learning models on labelled sentences drawn from inter-linked multilingual documents and machine translation data, so it can identify and classify such names across many languages and enrich the text with related information.

US2015292894.headline: Driving directions with confidence in arrival time
US2015292894.summary: Journey time estimates are often wrong because conditions change. This routing engine works out several routes to a destination, predicts the travel time for each using data on weather and other environmental factors affecting traffic, and also estimates how likely each prediction is to be accurate.

US2015309828.headline: Managing many types of virtual servers at once
US2015309828.summary: Data centres often run virtual machines on hypervisors from different vendors, each managed separately. An adaptive virtual server monitors how much each virtual machine uses and reallocates resources dynamically, even drawing on several hypervisors of different types, to improve utilisation and performance.

US2015333775.headline: Efficient decoding for a new error-correcting code
US2015333775.summary: Polar codes are a modern way of protecting transmitted data from errors, but efficient decoders are hard to build. This method derives the pattern of fixed bits from a decoder with a different internal wiring so that a simpler, time-shared decoder with fixed connections can still achieve strong performance.

US2015371135.headline: Planning delivery routes that adapt to road changes
US2015371135.summary: Working out the best routes for a fleet of vehicles is a notoriously hard problem, especially when roads close or conditions change. This method inserts placeholder nodes into the route map when changes occur and solves the problem with a hybrid of ant-colony and genetic algorithms.

US2015379429.headline: Interactive tool for judging prediction models
US2015379429.summary: Users of machine-learning services need to understand how good a model's predictions are. This interface displays quality metrics from an evaluation run and lets the user slide a threshold that decides how predictions are interpreted, showing immediately how the quality measures change.

US2015379848.headline: Turning sensor alerts into useful notifications
US2015379848.summary: Buildings and sites may have many sensors producing alerts of different kinds. This system gathers alerts from multiple sensor types, works out which events they indicate, decides whether a notification is warranted and sends it to the relevant parties, cutting down on noise.

US2016004628.headline: Testing websites on many browsers at once
US2016004628.summary: Websites must work across many browsers, and testing each in turn is slow. A server takes a selection of test scripts and target browsers, instructs client machines to launch the browsers, distributes the scripts to run in parallel and collects the results.

US2016011845.headline: One-click screen sharing from a chat
US2016011845.summary: Switching from a text chat to showing your screen usually means opening another application. Here a button in the chat window starts a screen-sharing session; the other participants receive an invitation message in their chat and, on accepting, see the shared screen without leaving the conversation.

US2016026579.headline: Faster bookkeeping for storage caches
US2016026579.summary: A cache that holds frequently used data in fast memory must track what is stored where and what has changed. This controller uses a mathematical mapping between data locations and the cache, plus compact bitmaps of recent use and modifications, to manage this metadata efficiently.

US2016028551.headline: Secure hardware that vouches for connected devices
US2016028551.summary: Internet-connected devices need trusted credentials but often lack the power for heavy cryptography. A certificate authority running inside a tamper-resistant hardware security module issues each device a certificate, then takes over its key management and encryption tasks once it has authenticated.

US2016036441.headline: Protecting delicate transistors when shifting voltages
US2016036441.summary: Signals that move into a higher-voltage part of a chip can stress components beyond their safe limits. This circuit adds tracking elements that cap the voltage across sensitive parts, and compensates for the delay they introduce so the output still switches on time.

US2016049658.headline: Cooler-running sodium-sulphur battery
US2016049658.summary: Conventional sodium-sulphur batteries operate at very high temperatures, creating heat management and sealing problems. This design pairs a sodium anode and a sulphur cathode with a liquid electrolyte and a solid sodium-conducting membrane, aiming to deliver good charge and discharge performance at lower temperatures.

US2016057596.headline: Phone distress signal on multiple radio bands
US2016057596.summary: A person in trouble may be out of range of one network but not another. This app turns a mobile phone into a distress beacon that broadcasts simultaneously over several radio protocols and frequency bands, increasing the chance the signal is picked up.

US2016058872.headline: Drugs that make cells destroy target proteins
US2016058872.summary: Many disease-causing proteins cannot be blocked by conventional drugs. These two-ended molecules attach one end to the cell's own protein-disposal machinery and the other to a chosen target protein, bringing them together so the cell breaks the target down, potentially offering a route to treat a wide range of conditions.

US2016062947.headline: Faster image processing for neural networks
US2016062947.summary: Convolution, the core calculation in image-recognition neural networks, is computationally heavy. This engine splits the work into image tiles processed independently on a parallel chip, assembling each tile in on-chip memory only as needed and multiplying it with filter data, saving both memory and time.

US2016079613.headline: Air-cooled housing for fuel cell electronics
US2016079613.summary: Electronics in fuel cell systems need cooling but some parts should be kept away from moving air. This housing is split by a heat exchanger into two compartments: a fan blows air through one, while the other remains still, so all components are cooled without exposing sensitive parts to airflow.

US2016085290.headline: Preventing power overload in fast storage drives
US2016085290.summary: High-speed memory drives connected directly to a computer can draw more power than their slot allows. This method monitors the drive's state, checks whether a new operation would push power over a preset limit and, if so, delays it while existing operations continue.

US2016085575.headline: Restarting a backed-up virtual machine in minutes
US2016085575.summary: Restoring a virtual machine from backup normally means waiting for all its data to be copied back. This system starts the machine almost immediately from pre-staged blocks in the backup store, predicting which data it will need first, while the rest is moved to primary storage in the background.

US2016095110.headline: Wi-Fi and mobile networks sharing airwaves politely
US2016095110.summary: Mobile operators increasingly use unlicensed radio bands that Wi-Fi also relies on, risking interference. Here a Wi-Fi access point reports which channels are busy, the mobile base station picks a free one and announces its transmission, and the Wi-Fi point tells its devices to stay off that channel meanwhile.

US2016099010.headline: Combined neural network for speech recognition
US2016099010.summary: Transcribing speech accurately is difficult. This approach feeds audio features through a model that stacks three kinds of neural network layers, convolutional, long short-term memory and fully connected, to produce a transcription, and can also identify the language being spoken.

US2016105321.headline: Moving virtual machines to the cloud intact
US2016105321.summary: Shifting a virtual machine from a company's own data centre to a public cloud risks losing the infrastructure settings it depends on. This method records those configurations and how critical each is, bundles them into a migration package, and the cloud recreates the machine to match.

US2016148079.headline: Faster face detection in photos
US2016148079.summary: Finding faces or other objects in an image means checking many candidate regions. This method passes those regions through a chain of neural networks, each quickly discarding regions that clearly contain no object, so only promising candidates reach the slower, more accurate later stages.

US2016169142.headline: Fine-tuning fuel mix in dual-fuel engines
US2016169142.summary: Engines that burn two fuels, such as diesel and natural gas, need the right blend in each cylinder. This method estimates the temperature inside each cylinder from exhaust residuals, manifold conditions and fuel quantity, then sets how much of the first fuel to replace with the second, cylinder by cylinder.

US2016182565.headline: Network access rules based on where you are
US2016182565.summary: Companies may want certain data available only from particular places. This security device works out the geographical location of a device requesting access and checks it against location-specific rules for the resource before deciding whether to allow the request.

US2016188245.headline: Memory cards that start up at low voltage
US2016188245.summary: Some host devices send their first commands to a memory card at a lower voltage than the card's circuitry expects. This system detects that situation and switches the card's voltage regulator into a low-voltage mode so it can receive the start-up commands correctly.

US2016191568.headline: Seeing which apps are using the network
US2016191568.summary: Network administrators often cannot tell which applications are generating traffic, by whom and from where. This architecture copies selected traffic flows to an application-identification tool, starting small and growing to cover the whole network, and uses the results to set and enforce usage policies.

US2016213673.headline: Supplement to boost physical endurance
US2016213673.summary: Athletes and active people seek safe ways to sustain effort. This formulation combines dihydrocapsiate, a compound derived from chilli peppers, with caffeine and the amino acid arginine, and is claimed to increase human endurance during physical activity.

US2016231716.headline: Simulating industrial systems for better business decisions
US2016231716.summary: Running connected industrial assets involves trade-offs between physical performance and commercial results. This system generates scenarios from chosen criteria, simulates both the physical and business outcomes of each over time, and picks the scenario that best balances performance and risk.

US2016261727.headline: Switching live data streams between data centres
US2016261727.summary: Streams of database updates must keep flowing even when one data centre has to hand over to another. This method performs such a switchover while notifying each component in the chain, so processing continues without losing or duplicating data.

US2016266894.headline: Updating network device software without downtime
US2016266894.summary: Updating the firmware on a router or switch usually means restarting it and interrupting traffic. This method replaces the firmware on one group of processor cores at a time while the others keep handling packets, until every core is running the new version with no reset.

US2016281607.headline: Smarter start-up for combined-cycle power plants
US2016281607.summary: Starting a combined-cycle power plant is a delicate, costly process. This method collects start-up measurements from many similar plants, derives reference relationships between operating parameters, and uses them to benchmark and adjust the start-up of a target plant.

US2016299767.headline: Network card that can boot the server itself
US2016299767.summary: Servers in storage networks normally boot their operating system from remote storage. This adapter includes its own non-volatile memory holding a boot image; data addressed to that memory is kept locally while other data goes to the network, and at power-up the server can boot directly from the card.

US2016328674.headline: Filling orders from the nearest warehouse with stock
US2016328674.summary: Retailers selling through many channels struggle to fulfil orders when the main warehouse is out of stock. This system checks the primary hub first, then consults a cache of stock at secondary hubs, chooses one by proximity to the delivery address and priority, and places a backorder if none can supply.

US2016342491.headline: Spreading backup copies across many servers
US2016342491.summary: Storage systems built from many nodes must decide where to keep data and its redundant copies. Here every node holds configuration information on data placement, and any node can take the lead in recalculating that layout when the redundancy policy changes.

US2016342501.headline: Speeding up automated software testing
US2016342501.summary: Writing automated tests for software screens is laborious. This system records a script of a screen to identify its input fields, chooses test-case templates based on sample input, gathers the needed data sets and checks, and assembles them into an executable test that produces a report.

US2016350653.headline: One neural network for many language tasks
US2016350653.summary: Different language-processing tasks usually require separate systems. This framework recasts every task, from translation to sentiment, as answering a question about an input text, building memories from the input and question and generating answers from those memories.

US2016364608.headline: Automatically pulling key information from long documents
US2016364608.summary: Extracting specific details from lengthy documents such as contracts is slow manual work. This pipeline recognises a document's structure, splits it into sections, classifies and maps them to key elements, drills into sub-sections with machine learning, and presents the extracted information in a navigable interface.

US2016364857.headline: Learning which medical images lead to a diagnosis
US2016364857.summary: Radiologists view many images in a study but base their diagnosis on only some. This system records characteristics of each image and whether it was used to reach the diagnosis, building a dataset that can reveal which image features matter for a given type of study.

US2016378168.headline: Smarter power saving for processor cores
US2016378168.summary: Mobile processors waste power keeping cores active when little is happening. This power manager tracks how many cores are busy and how hard they work, takes cores offline when averages fall below thresholds, wakes them only periodically for background updates, and shuts cores down if the device gets too hot.

US2017004513.headline: Predicting which subscribers will cancel
US2017004513.summary: Subscription businesses want to know who is about to leave. This system selects the most informative customer attributes from historical data, builds a decision tree from them and applies it to current subscribers to flag those likely to churn.

US2017024645.headline: One neural network for many language tasks
US2017024645.summary: Different language-processing tasks usually require separate systems. This framework recasts every task as answering a question about an input text, building memories from the input and question and generating answers from those dynamically retrieved memories.

US2017024864.headline: Removing unwanted objects from photos convincingly
US2017024864.summary: Erasing an object from a picture leaves a gap that must be filled plausibly. This method aligns several photos of the same scene from different viewpoints, builds a library of image patches from them, and reconstructs the gap by combining the best-matching patches.

US2017060653.headline: Apps that report when they misbehave
US2017060653.summary: Companies struggle to know how their apps actually perform on users' devices. This method wraps the app so that it reports performance metrics for each operating state to a central computer, which checks them against rules and sends a response back when something is out of line.

US2017061250.headline: Matching pictures to words automatically
US2017061250.summary: Searching images by text, or captioning them, requires understanding how pictures and sentences relate. This framework maps both into a shared semantic space using a deep learning model, judges their relevance by closeness, and can output the best-matching sentence as a caption.

US2017062851.headline: Fuel cell stacks that warn of trouble early
US2017062851.summary: Problems in a fuel cell stack can spread before they are detected. This design gives the cells at the ends of the stack a lower fuel flow and higher air flow than the rest, making them more sensitive so adverse conditions show up there first and can be acted on.

US2017072876.headline: Faster translation between car networks
US2017072876.summary: Modern cars contain several incompatible internal networks that must exchange messages. This gateway uses dedicated hardware to filter packets, look up headers and bundle messages, translating between the different bus standards far faster than software alone.

US2017116693.headline: Blockchain record of who may play digital media
US2017116693.summary: Managing rights to films, music and other digital content usually depends on a central authority. This system records licences on a shared blockchain ledger; a playback device finds the licence matching its own identity, decrypts the content key with its private key and plays the content.

US2017123935.headline: Organising files for efficient cloud backup
US2017123935.summary: Businesses use fast file storage for daily work but cheaper object storage for backups. This layout represents folders and files as metadata objects in object storage, with file data stored as elements of data objects, making snapshots and de-duplication of backups more efficient.

US2017126314.headline: Squeezing more traffic through optical networks
US2017126314.summary: Optical fibre networks often reserve more capacity than traffic actually uses. This method samples bandwidth use over time on ports and links, monitors statistical measures of it, and triggers adjustments to traffic or routing when patterns allow, so capacity is shared more efficiently.

US2017173879.headline: 3D printer nozzle with adjustable openings
US2017173879.summary: Standard 3D printer nozzles extrude a fixed stream of material. This nozzle has several concentric rings at its tip that can be opened or closed during printing to vary how much material comes out or to mix materials, giving finer control over the printed object.

US2017176985.headline: Predicting product quality before final inspection
US2017176985.summary: Manufacturers usually find defects only at final inspection. This method tests sub-components earlier, investigates which of their attributes drive lower final quality, builds and validates prediction models from those attributes and forecasts the end-of-line quality of each assembled product.

US2017206431.headline: Quickly finding and naming objects in images
US2017206431.summary: Identifying what objects are in a picture and where is central to computer vision. This method generates a feature map from the image, proposes candidate regions likely to hold objects, then classifies each region and reports the object type with a confidence score.

US2017235662.headline: A single quality score for software applications
US2017235662.summary: Judging the overall quality of an application means weighing many factors. This method collects data on functional aspects, what the software does, and non-functional aspects such as performance and security, from several sources, scores each and combines them into one quality score.

US2017236060.headline: Spotting mistakes in data as it is typed
US2017236060.summary: Typing errors and wrong entries creep into databases and are costly to find later. This system uses statistics and machine learning to flag entries that look suspicious, either as they are being typed in or in records that were stored earlier, so they can be checked and corrected.

US2017236081.headline: Mapping who really talks to whom at work
US2017236081.summary: Official organisation charts rarely show how information actually flows in a company. This tool builds a picture of the organisation from real communication patterns, drawing staff as connected nodes where the links reflect how often and about what people interact, helping managers see influence, bottlenecks and involvement in decisions.

US2017269980.headline: Predicting when storage drives will fail
US2017269980.summary: Solid-state drives in large storage systems fail without much warning, which can disrupt services. This method keeps watch on health reports, workloads and response times, combines them to estimate how close each drive is to failure, and recommends replacing drives in a cost-effective order before a serious breakdown occurs.

US2017270765.headline: Fitness tracker shows messages when you move
US2017270765.summary: Fitness bands have small screens and limited battery, so showing messages constantly is wasteful. This approach downloads messages to the device and displays one only when the wearer moves after being still, such as lifting the wrist, so messages appear when the person is likely to look.

US2017272458.headline: Machine learning to catch network intruders
US2017272458.summary: Cyber attacks increasingly evade traditional defences that only look for known threats. This security platform analyses large volumes of network data and learns the normal behaviour of users and devices, flagging unusual activity both instantly and in periodic deeper reviews, and presents risk scores with evidence so administrators can act quickly.

US2017286572.headline: A virtual copy that monitors real equipment
US2017286572.summary: Industrial equipment is costly to inspect and failures are disruptive. This system keeps a digital twin, a computer model of a physical machine fed by its sensors, that tracks the condition of chosen parts and estimates their remaining useful life, even while the machine is switched off, then reports the findings.

US2017286979.headline: Predicting which media files people will download
US2017286979.summary: Online libraries hold far more files than anyone can browse. This method summarises each media file as a data profile, compares it with similar files whose download history is known, and produces a score estimating how likely users are to download it, helping decide what to promote or store.

US2017291301.headline: Teaching robots to navigate by example
US2017291301.summary: Programming robots to find their way around is laborious. This approach lets a robot learn on the job: as a trainer guides it, the robot links what its sensors see to the control actions taken, and gradually predicts the right moves itself. The learning runs on board in real time, enabling autonomous navigation.

US2017302431.headline: Keeping fast data links in step
US2017302431.summary: When data travels at very high speed over several parallel lines, signals can arrive slightly out of step and corrupt the message. This transceiver design re-times, combines and separates data streams to keep them aligned, allowing reliable high-speed connections between computers, storage and peripheral devices.

US2017315838.headline: Choosing the best server for a moving workload
US2017315838.summary: Data centres often shift virtual machines between servers for maintenance or balancing. This method scores each candidate server on how well it meets the workload's operating requirements and uses the scores to pick the most suitable destination, making migrations smoother.

US2017329332.headline: Self-driving car judges if objects will interfere
US2017329332.summary: Self-driving cars must decide how to react to pedestrians, cyclists and other vehicles nearby. This control system uses sensor data about the road ahead to estimate the probability that a detected object will cross the car's planned path, then adjusts speed or route according to that likelihood.

US2018067565.headline: Recognising who is wearing a fitness tracker
US2018067565.summary: Fitness trackers cannot easily tell whether the right person is wearing them. This method identifies the wearer from the device's own data, combining the pattern of their movements with the shape of their heartbeat signal, which could help secure personal data or detect when the tracker is shared.

US2018071918.headline: Home robot that works around household activity
US2018071918.summary: Household robots can be disruptive if they run while people are busy. This robot maps the home, connects to the home network, notices which connected devices are present and whether they are active or idle, and starts or pauses its chores, such as cleaning, accordingly.

US2018089042.headline: Cutting data centre costs by predicting failures
US2018089042.summary: Servers and hard drives in data centres wear out faster in hot, humid or corrosive conditions. This system monitors the environment, estimates when each piece of equipment is likely to fail, and weighs replacement, running and downtime costs to minimise total cost of ownership and energy use.

US2018121766.headline: Smarter task allocation in call centres
US2018121766.summary: Call centres must constantly decide which agent or automated system should handle each enquiry. This system uses reinforcement learning to build a model of how the centre behaves under uncertainty and then uses that model to choose and assign work items to staff and machines more effectively.

US2018146015.headline: Merging multiple internet connections into one
US2018146015.summary: Modern devices can send data over several connections at once, such as Wi-Fi and mobile, but many servers cannot handle this. This method lets an intermediary device track the separate streams, renumber their packets consistently, and pass everything to the server as a single ordinary connection.

US2018149333.headline: Slimmer, brighter car lights
US2018149333.summary: Car lights must be compact yet put most of their light where it is needed. This lighting module uses a thin silicone lens whose entry surface gathers at least 69 per cent of the light into a parallel beam, while a patterned exit surface shapes it into the required pattern.

US2018152425.headline: Keeping Wi-Fi broadcast traffic within groups
US2018152425.summary: On a shared Wi-Fi network, broadcast messages intended for one group of users can be seen by everyone. This method gives each group its own encryption key, so broadcast messages are scrambled and can only be read by devices belonging to that group, improving privacy and security.

US2018190265.headline: Removing bad samples to improve synthetic speech
US2018190265.summary: Text-to-speech systems sound unnatural when the recordings used to train them are badly matched to their transcripts. This method automatically detects misaligned or mispronounced segments using features of pitch and timing, and removes them, so the resulting synthetic voice is clearer.

US2018229856.headline: Monitoring aircraft between landing and take-off
US2018229856.summary: Aircraft turnaround at the gate is a tight, costly window where problems are easy to miss. This system pulls operational readings from the aircraft's on-board systems during turnaround, checks them against expected ranges and raises alerts when something is out of line.

US2018246173.headline: Estimating lead-acid battery charge and health live
US2018246173.summary: Knowing how much charge remains in a lead-acid battery, and how worn it is, is hard to measure directly. This method uses regular voltage, current and temperature readings with a lightweight mathematical model and filtering to estimate charge in real time and update the battery's health after each charge or discharge.

US2018251037.headline: Built-in jumper cable for flat batteries
US2018251037.summary: Drivers with a flat battery often lack jumper cables. This vehicle has a retractable cable with a plug stored in a compartment on the bodywork; when pulled out it connects directly to another vehicle's socket to give or receive a jump start.

US2018253256.headline: Measuring how applications use shared storage
US2018253256.summary: In large data centres it is hard to see how individual applications are performing on shared storage networks. This method monitors read and write commands passing through the network hardware, calculates detailed performance measures for each application, and uses them to choose the most suitable storage device.

US2018285798.headline: Learning from past IT incidents to fix outages
US2018285798.summary: IT operations teams face floods of alerts and repeat the same troubleshooting. This system groups past events into clusters, attaches how each was resolved, and trains models that predict the likely fix for new live events, retraining when accuracy slips.

US2018330088.headline: Protecting backups from ransomware
US2018330088.summary: Ransomware can encrypt files and then be copied into backups, destroying the clean versions. This backup system watches for unusual changes across many devices or on a single device compared with normal behaviour, and when it suspects an attack it locks or preserves earlier snapshots so clean copies survive.

US2018332055.headline: Putting security rules in the best order
US2018332055.summary: Network firewalls apply long lists of rules, and where a new rule sits in the list affects how well threats are caught. This system lets administrators create rules from a visual display and automatically works out the best position for each one based on detected anomalies and threat data.

US2019004504.headline: Predicting chip defects with deep learning
US2019004504.summary: Finding defects in semiconductor wafers by inspection alone is slow and expensive. This method uses initial inspection results, design details and manufacturing settings to train a deep learning model, refines it until predictions are accurate enough, and then uses it to predict where new defects are likely to appear.

US2019028407.headline: Keeping priority workloads to their service levels
US2019028407.summary: In shared data centres, important workloads must receive the network performance they were promised. This method collects performance data over time, tracks both short-term and long-term trends, and uses them to make sure high-priority workloads, and all workloads overall, stay within their quality-of-service targets.

US2019042559.headline: Decoding ambiguous references in medical notes
US2019042559.summary: Medical records are full of pronouns and references such as 'it' or 'this' whose meaning is ambiguous for computers. This program uses medical knowledge about related terms to work out which earlier entity each such reference points to, helping software read clinical text more accurately.

US2019042923.headline: Faster hardware for neural network calculations
US2019042923.summary: Neural networks rely heavily on a calculation called convolution, which is computationally demanding. This hardware accelerator uses a shortcut technique known as Winograd convolution and can reuse the same arrangement for different filter sizes, speeding up machine learning tasks.

US2019049975.headline: Sharing warehouse jobs among robots efficiently
US2019049975.summary: Warehouses with many robots must divide up collection tasks without a central bottleneck. This method breaks an overall job into sub-tasks, considers robot availability and cost constraints, and lets the robots negotiate the allocation among themselves with light coordination, so work is completed efficiently.

US2019163254.headline: Quicker wake-up from processor sleep mode
US2019163254.summary: Powering down a processor saves energy, but waking it fully takes time. This technique turns off the processing cores of a chip such as a graphics processor while keeping its data link interface powered, so the chip saves energy yet resumes work much faster than existing approaches.

US2019168206.headline: Longer-lasting catalyst for making syngas
US2019168206.summary: Converting carbon dioxide and methane into synthetic gas needs catalysts that usually degrade at high temperatures or require precious metals. This catalyst coats the active material on a metal oxide support and surrounds it with a surfactant, which stops it clumping or being coated in carbon, so it stays active for long periods.

US2019188584.headline: Predicting equipment failures in industrial plants
US2019188584.summary: Industrial plants record vast numbers of measurements, making it hard to build reliable failure predictors. This system cleans the data, removes uninformative variables, adds useful derived measures, selects the most relevant inputs and trains a model that then runs live to detect and predict equipment failures.

US2019189356.headline: More reliable miniature capacitors
US2019189356.summary: Multilayer ceramic capacitors are tiny components found in almost all electronics. This design adjusts the composition of the protective side margins, using less silicon in the layer nearest the internal electrodes, which is intended to improve the component's reliability.

US2019190386.headline: Power supply that switches stages on demand
US2019190386.summary: Power regulators that use several parallel stages waste energy when demand is low. This circuit compares the output against a threshold and automatically switches a second stage on or off as needed, improving efficiency across varying loads.

US2019194092.headline: More propylene from oil refineries
US2019194092.summary: Propylene, a key raw material for plastics, is in high demand. This process links a refinery's catalytic cracking unit with a step that converts leftover propane into propylene and other light olefins, using carbon dioxide from the cracker's own flue gas, boosting yields of valuable chemicals.

US2019197420.headline: Compressing neural network data on the fly
US2019197420.summary: Neural networks shuffle huge volumes of data between processors and memory, which slows them down. This design adds a hardware encoder and decoder to the memory transfer unit so the data is compressed as it is written and decompressed when read, saving bandwidth and energy.

US2019207568.headline: Amplifier for ultra-fast fibre optic links
US2019207568.summary: Fibre optic receivers must convert very faint light signals into clean electrical ones at speeds of 400 gigabits per second. This amplifier design, built with standard chip manufacturing, uses a dual-mode arrangement that works across a range of voltages, supporting faster and cheaper optical links.

US2019217755.headline: Smarter-looking car seat back
US2019217755.summary: The back of a car seat is often plain and hard to refurbish. This backrest fixes a hard panel to the seat frame and wraps it in a decorative cover whose edges are joined by a fastener, so the panel looks attractive and the cover can be opened or replaced.

US2019220967.headline: Automatically spotting changes in images over time
US2019220967.summary: Detecting change in images taken of the same place over time, such as farmland, normally needs laboriously labelled training data. This method uses a general-purpose image recognition network to extract features, groups images without labels, and combines this with classification for real-time analysis, even offline at the edge.

US2019222560.headline: One search across many secure data stores
US2019222560.summary: Organisations keep documents in many separate systems, forcing users to search each one. This method runs a single search across several stores that the user is authorised to access, gathers the results from each and merges them into one combined set of results.

US2019278663.headline: Backups scheduled to meet recovery targets
US2019278663.summary: Firms set targets for how much data they can afford to lose, but backup schedules are usually configured by hand. This system asks for fewer settings, schedules backups automatically to meet the target, raises the priority of failed items and retries only those, so the recovery goal is met.

US2019278921.headline: Tamper-proof recordings of phone calls
US2019278921.summary: Recorded conversations are only useful as evidence if they cannot be altered. This system records voice communications, uses an authentication server to verify their validity and timestamps them, storing the recordings in a database so their integrity can be trusted.

US2019280514.headline: Car stops charging your phone when full
US2019280514.summary: Leaving a phone plugged into a car charger keeps topping it up unnecessarily. This system detects when a phone is connected, charges it, then uses a Bluetooth link to read the battery level and switches charging off when it is high enough and back on when it drops below a lower level.

US2019319868.headline: Forecasting mobile network quality ahead of time
US2019319868.summary: Apps and networks perform better if they know in advance when a connection will slow down or drop. This system predicts future link performance, such as bandwidth, delay and coverage gaps, by combining results from several analysis layers and shares the forecasts with apps and network equipment.

US2019340588.headline: Blockchain record of shared ownership of devices
US2019340588.summary: Shared ownership of connected devices, such as a jointly owned car or appliance, is hard to track and enforce. This system records fractional ownership and usage rights on a secure blockchain ledger, applies encrypted rules when events occur, updates stakes accordingly and monitors whether owners respect usage limits.

US2019340945.headline: Personalised learning paths towards a career goal
US2019340945.summary: People seeking a new career rarely know which skills to learn in what order. This method builds a map of which skills depend on which, identifies the skills needed for a target job and their prerequisites, and generates a personalised sequence of courses and materials for the individual.

US2019347668.headline: One customer record for sales, marketing and service
US2019347668.summary: Businesses often hold scattered, inconsistent records of the same customer across departments. This platform keeps a single universal contact record for each person in one database, with attributes usable for sales, marketing, service and content activities, and offers improved tools for those functions built on it.

US2019370123.headline: Copying live data to a backup computer
US2019370123.summary: Businesses need a standby copy of their systems to recover quickly after a disaster. This method replicates data blocks from a running computer to a backup machine while the data is still changing, and can also replicate from a recovery machine that was itself built from a protected system.

US2019385043.headline: Training AI on phones without sharing private data
US2019385043.summary: Training machine learning models usually means collecting users' data centrally, raising privacy concerns. Here a server sends a shared model to devices, some of which improve it using their own data and send back only the suggested parameter changes, never the raw data, which the server combines to update the model.

US2019386916.headline: Choosing network routes with timing in mind
US2019386916.summary: Some network traffic needs routers whose clocks are precisely synchronised. This method lets the system that computes routes take into account the synchronisation status of each router when a path is requested, and returns a route that meets the requirement.

US2020089650.headline: Automatically cleaning data for machine learning
US2020089650.summary: Machine learning needs clean data, but tidying up missing or messy values is usually done by hand. This method describes each variable with summary features, feeds them to pre-trained models that recommend how to fill gaps and preprocess the data, applies those steps automatically and builds a better model.

US2020097703.headline: Scoring how striking a photo is
US2020097703.summary: Sorting large photo collections benefits from knowing which pictures have most impact. This method detects faces in an image, scores each one on features such as size or expression, weights and combines the scores, and stores an overall impact score for the picture.

US2020112487.headline: Safely testing new software versions with live traffic
US2020112487.summary: Rolling out a new version of a software service risks breaking things for users. This method copies real incoming traffic, analyses its patterns, and sends simulated traffic matching those patterns to the new version, then compares performance measurements of old and new versions before deciding to switch.

US2020133658.headline: Blockchain for approving software code changes
US2020133658.summary: Changes to a software project's source code need to be reviewed and traceable. This method treats each change as a transaction that must be validated by several contributors on a decentralised network and records it as a block in a blockchain, creating a tamper-resistant history.

US2020160356.headline: Reading customer emotions to improve service
US2020160356.summary: Companies struggle to make sense of what customers say about them across many channels. This system gathers direct and indirect customer communications, converts speech to text where needed, analyses sentiment and emotion, and displays the scores so managers can change products, fix service problems or target marketing.

US2020164762.headline: Helping electric cars find battery swap stations
US2020164762.summary: Electric vehicle drivers with low batteries need to find a place to swap them in time. This method reads the battery voltage, estimates remaining range, locates battery-swapping centres within reach when the level is low, and sends the centre information about the car's battery state.

US2020208887.headline: Water-cooled air conditioning condenser
US2020208887.summary: Air conditioning condensers work harder and use more energy when the air around them is hot. This design places a porous, water-soaked material in front of the condenser coil so incoming air is cooled by evaporation before reaching the coil, improving efficiency.

US2020210223.headline: Running software tasks without waiting around
US2020210223.summary: Complex software operations involve many steps, some of which call other services and would normally leave processors idle while waiting. This system arranges tasks as a graph, queues them to pools of workers in the right order, and makes calls to other services without blocking, so work keeps flowing.

US2020402044.headline: Letting appliances pay for things securely
US2020402044.summary: Connected appliances such as fridges could order supplies, but need a safe way to pay. This method registers an anonymous account to the appliance, gives it a payment token, links it later to the owner's account, and authorises transactions by checking the token against both accounts.

US2021012298.headline: Self-certifying payment terminals for card networks
US2021012298.summary: Before a payment terminal can process card transactions it must be certified, usually a slow manual process. This system lets the terminal send test transactions, compares the results with expected values automatically, and grants certification and authorisation to use the payment networks when they match.

US2021026982.headline: Finding sensitive data by sampling files
US2021026982.summary: Scanning every file in full to find personal or sensitive information is slow. This system analyses only part of each structured-data file, on the basis that if the sample contains no sensitive data the rest usually does not, and adjusts data management jobs to comply with privacy rules.

US2021065391.headline: Building 3D maps from a single ordinary camera
US2021065391.summary: Mapping surroundings in three dimensions usually requires special depth sensors. This method takes video from a single ordinary camera, uses a neural network to estimate depth for each frame, and combines the images and depth estimates to work out the camera's position and build a 3D map.

US2021073026.headline: Checking and publishing automated workflows
US2021073026.summary: Automated workflows written by one team can be useful to others but may be unreliable. This system receives a workflow over a network, tests it by running or analysing its steps, checks it meets publishing criteria, and if so stores it in a repository for other systems to use.

US2021073377.headline: Reusing trained AI to detect new cyber threats
US2021073377.summary: Training a threat detector from scratch for every file type needs lots of labelled examples. This method trains a model on one type of file, then transfers some of its learned layers to a second model trained on a different type, so the knowledge carries over and threats in the new domain are detected.

US2021089822.headline: Teaching software which content types are similar
US2021089822.summary: Content suggestion systems work better when they understand that some content types are more alike than others. This technique learns numerical representations of content types in which similar types sit close together, and uses them as features to improve suggestions to users.

US2021107141.headline: Plugging AI models into office automation
US2021107141.summary: Software robots that automate office tasks are hard to combine with machine learning models from different sources. This framework offers a drag-and-drop interface and a managed process for uploading, validating, publishing and deploying models, including versioning, so they slot into automated workflows.

US2021108505.headline: Measuring the energy content of well fluids
US2021108505.summary: Knowing the heat content of fluids flowing in a well, such as in geothermal or oil operations, is difficult. This downhole tool heats the fluid until it becomes a single phase, senses that transition, and uses the power consumed by the heater to calculate the fluid's enthalpy.

US2021208615.headline: Steadier output voltage from chip connections
US2021208615.summary: Chips must deliver reliable voltages at their output pins despite varying conditions. This circuit monitors the pin's voltage as feedback and combines it with two reference voltages to generate tracking signals that control the output, keeping the voltage stable.

US2021266185.headline: Home router that filters encrypted web lookups
US2021266185.summary: Encrypted domain name lookups protect privacy but stop home routers applying parental controls or blocking malicious sites. This router handles the encrypted lookups itself using its own certificate, decrypts the request, checks it against stored rules and acts accordingly.

US2021398496.headline: Smoother screen brightness changes
US2021398496.summary: Rapid changes in screen backlight, for example when brightness adjusts automatically, can be distracting to the eye. This technology generates a compensation signal from user and system inputs and passes it through a filter to smooth fast transitions, adjusting brightness in a way that suits human vision.

US2022058090.headline: Backups that run when the moment is right
US2022058090.summary: Backups run on fixed schedules even when the system is busy or data has barely changed. This approach calculates a readiness score from a number of operational factors, launches backups when conditions are favourable, and learns from recent jobs which factors matter most, adjusting their weights over time.

US2022066839.headline: Controlling which chip cores access devices
US2022066839.summary: In a chip with several processor cores, not every core should be able to control every attached device. This circuit keeps lock bits for each byte of a device's control registers and grants access at two levels, based on which core is asking and which bytes it wants, improving security.

US2022078090.headline: Tracing a user's slow connection step by step
US2022078090.summary: When a remote worker reports a slow connection, IT staff struggle to find the cause. This cloud-based technique lets an administrator start a detailed trace from the user's device to the destination, collects results and device metrics, and shows a map of the network path between them.

US2022086234.headline: Resetting database sessions cheaply
US2022086234.summary: Opening a fresh database connection for every request is clean but slow. This technique detects when an application has finished a unit of work, checks that the session is at a safe point, and resets it so it behaves like a new session without the cost of creating one, avoiding leaks of state between requests.

US2022100813.headline: Reconfigurable chip for matrix maths
US2022100813.summary: Matrix and vector calculations underpin AI and graphics, but fixed hardware layouts suit only some matrix shapes. This processor arranges computing elements in rows and columns and maps memory connections to them dynamically according to the dimensions of the matrices being processed, so it adapts to different jobs.

US2022120367.headline: Rotating joint for hydraulic hoses
US2022120367.summary: Hydraulic hoses on machinery can twist and wear where moving parts meet. This swivel joint receives fluid in one direction and can redirect it before it exits, using two repositionable connectors on a base so hoses can be routed flexibly.

US2022121528.headline: Backing up large storage volumes in slices
US2022121528.summary: Backing up very large block storage devices in one piece is slow and fragile. This system measures the device, splits it into slices, records where each slice is stored in a lookup table, and uses multiple backup agents to copy the slices in parallel to network storage as snapshots.

US2022207988.headline: Automatic fixes for recurring plant alarms
US2022207988.summary: Industrial control rooms are swamped with alarms, many of which recur in familiar sequences. This method identifies patterns in the alarm log, recognises when a new alarm fits a known pattern, works out the actions that resolved it before and carries them out.

US2022250906.headline: Tougher catalyst for hydrogen production
US2022250906.summary: Catalysts used in the first stage of making hydrogen from hydrocarbons can be damaged when exposed to steam alone. This nickel oxide catalyst with a small amount of platinum resists such deactivation, making the production of hydrogen or hydrogen-rich gas more robust.

US2022414818.headline: Saving memory when drawing 3D graphics
US2022414818.summary: Graphics processors store references to every corner of the shapes they draw, and full memory addresses take up space. This technique replaces them with much shorter index numbers within a window of recent vertices and indicates when a full address is needed, reducing memory use.

US2023123775.headline: Cloud-style management for software-defined networks
US2023123775.summary: Modern applications run in containers managed by orchestration tools, but network configuration often sits outside that world. This architecture lets the network controller handle both standard container resources and custom network settings through the same kind of interface, and automatically applies changes when settings are updated.

US2023213997.headline: Slowing idle storage chip stages to save power
US2023213997.summary: Storage controllers process data in a series of stages that all usually run at full speed. This design measures how busy each stage is and gives slower stages a lower clock speed than the system clock, cutting power use without slowing the work.

US2023266899.headline: Switching memory boost features on by voltage
US2023266899.summary: Memory chips have performance features that only help under certain operating conditions. This system watches the supply voltage and turns the feature on when voltage crosses a threshold one way and off when it crosses back, allowing the feature to be used safely even in very large, complex chips.

US2023316629.headline: Faster realistic shadows in computer graphics
US2023316629.summary: Realistic shading in games requires calculating how much light each point receives, which is expensive with full ray tracing. This method first checks whether cheaper screen-based or probe-based lighting data is available in a given direction and only falls back to ray tracing when it is not.

US2023325173.headline: Personalised views of shared virtual storage
US2023325173.summary: In shared virtual computing environments, users should only see storage information relevant to them. This virtualised file server answers requests for storage details, such as how much space is available, with responses tailored to each user's own configuration and quota.

US2023326088.headline: Image compression keeping important parts sharp
US2023326088.summary: Standard compression squeezes all parts of an image equally. This method lets a user indicate which areas matter most and a target file size; a neural network learns an importance map from that guidance and compresses the image so the important regions keep more detail.

US2023327967.headline: Profiling normal network behaviour of each computer
US2023327967.summary: Detecting unusual network activity requires knowing what normal looks like. This method sorts measurements of a computer's traffic with a service into ranges, refines those ranges over time by merging and splitting them, and aggregates the results into a profile of typical behaviour.

US2023342552.headline: Better prompts for language models without retraining
US2023342552.summary: Adapting large language models to new tasks is costly if the model itself must be retrained. This technique generates small learned prompts that adapt to each input text and refines them with a discrete codebook, then feeds them with the text into a frozen model, improving understanding at low cost.

US2023362245.headline: Setting up private clusters in shared data centres
US2023362245.summary: Cloud customers want dedicated computing clusters with pooled storage, but configuring them by hand is complex. This method takes a cluster request, builds a secure private network overlay for the tenant, uses it to provision further networking, links the servers' local disks into one shared pool and configures the switches automatically.

US2023401088.headline: Automating deployment of interconnected microservices
US2023401088.summary: Modern applications consist of many small services with dependencies on one another, making deployment fiddly. This technique fetches the right configuration package and container images for the required services, creates a cluster and deploys the services with their dependencies set up automatically.

US2024048551.headline: Letting apps from new locations prove themselves
US2024048551.summary: Access to restricted systems is often limited to known network addresses, which blocks legitimate users elsewhere. This method issues a one-off registration secret through a second channel, checks a token signed with it, and then gives the device a communication secret it can use to access the resource.

US2024095993.headline: Fewer wasted calculations in ray tracing
US2024095993.summary: Ray tracing hardware speeds up realistic rendering but often tests rays against bounding boxes they do not really hit. These techniques reduce such false positives by re-testing with higher precision where needed, discarding boxes that have shrunk to a point, and clipping rays beyond set distances.

US2024163188.headline: Measuring network delay from packet numbers
US2024163188.summary: Knowing how long a packet takes to travel to its destination and back helps diagnose network problems. This system records a packet's details, works out the acknowledgement number it should receive, and when a matching acknowledgement arrives, calculates the round-trip time from the two timestamps.

US2024214383.headline: Spotting unusual user access rights
US2024214383.summary: Organisations find it hard to notice when an employee's system access looks out of place. This AI system builds a graph of identities and their access rights, groups similar users into peer groups, and flags those whose patterns differ from their peers as potential risks.

US2024288667.headline: Eight-element camera lens for phones
US2024288667.summary: Compact cameras in phones and other devices need high image quality in little space. This lens assembly arranges eight lens elements in three groups with specific shapes and curvatures, including specially curved final elements, to achieve sharper images in a slim unit.

US2024378117.headline: One backup snapshot covering several applications
US2024378117.summary: Taking consistent backups when several applications share the same storage is tricky. This system checks with each application's agent that it is in a stable state, takes a single snapshot of the shared volume, and records which part of the snapshot belongs to which application for easy restoration.

US2025250982.headline: Keeping pumps running at peak efficiency
US2025250982.summary: Pumps and similar machines waste energy when run away from their most efficient speed. This controller estimates the motor's torque and speed, compares them with stored performance data to find the current operating point, checks how far it is from the best efficiency point, and decides whether to change speed.

US2025258680.headline: Central control panel for scattered business software
US2025258680.summary: Large organisations run many different services spread across their systems, each configured separately. This system provides a single central place to configure a range of service types, including services run outside the cloud but linked to a cloud platform.
